content:
The [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert JSON to YAML — paste JSON, get clean YAML back. Enter your JSON and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert JSON to YAML: paste JSON and get the same data back as clean, two-space-indented YAML — the format configuration files, CI pipelines and Docker Compose expect. It is the reverse of the YAML to JSON converter: together they let you move data between the two formats in either direction. Invalid JSON returns a clear error instead of a half-converted result. Everything runs in your browser; your data is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the JSON to YAML Converter

Start by typing or pasting your JSON. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your JSON into the editor (or use the sample).
2. Click Convert — the YAML appears below.
3. Copy it into your configuration file.

## How it works

The [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Converting `{"site": {"name": "My Site"}}` gives `site:` followed by `  name: My Site`. Try the same figures in the [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What converts cleanly

Objects become indented mappings, arrays become dash lists, strings stay plain unless they need quoting, and numbers and booleans carry over unchanged. Values that would be ambiguous in YAML (a string that looks like a number, for example) are quoted automatically.

## When to use YAML instead of JSON

YAML is easier to read and write by hand, which is why configuration files use it. JSON is easier for machines to produce and parse, which is why APIs use it. Converting between them is a routine step when moving settings between systems.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Validate the JSON first — an error message names the problem.
- Use the YAML to JSON converter to go the other way.
- Check quoted values after converting — strings that look like numbers are quoted for safety.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does JSON to YAML do?

It converts JSON data into YAML — the same data, written with indentation instead of braces, which is easier to read and is what configuration files use. Try it with your own numbers in the [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### How do I convert YAML back to JSON?

Use the YAML to JSON converter on this site — the two tools are a pair. Try it with your own numbers in the [JSON to YAML Converter](/json-to-yaml-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the JSON to YAML Converter?

Just JSON. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
